newsitem.title: USA: NBA-BULLS THUMP BUCKS WITHOUT RODMAN.
newsitem.headline: NBA-BULLS THUMP BUCKS WITHOUT RODMAN.

text.p: Michael Jordan and Toni Kukoc scored 24 points apiece as the Chicago Bulls didn't miss a beat without suspended forward Dennis Rodman on Friday, thumping the Milwaukee Bucks 100-73.
Scottie Pippen added 20 points for the Bulls, who have won nine straight games and improved to an NBA-best of 34-4.
"We took too many outside shots and they were just too tough on us defensively," said Vin Baker, who led the Bucks with 36 points. "They were not going to be embarrassed without Rodman in the game."
Rodman was suspended until at least the All-Star break and fined $25,000 for kicking a cameraman in the Bulls' 112-102 victory at Minnesota on Wednesday.
"We played without Dennis before. You just have to go and suck it up, make the best of the situation," said Jordan about Rodman's absence.
"Some of our young players are really going to have a chance to contribute now, getting some important minutes in crucial situations. It's just going to make us a better team."

At Washington, Alonzo Mourning scored 34 points as the Miami Heat defeated the Washington Bullets for the second time in five days with a 103-92 victory in Baltimore that gave Miami the sole lead from New York in the Atlantic Division.
Voshon Lenard added 21 points for the Heat (28-10), who improved to a league-best 19-5 on the road.
Juwan Howard had a season-high 33 points for Washington, which has dropped three straight games. Chris Webber, who averages a team-leading 20.5 points, scored just four points.
In Vancouver, Karl Malone scored 10 of his 30 points in the third quarter as the Utah Jazz rolled to their biggest win of the season, a 106-68 demolition of the Vancouver Grizzlies.
Stephen Howard added 15 points for the Jazz, who stopped an eight-game road losing streak. Bryant Reeves scored 17 points for the Grizzlies.
In Portland, Damon Stoudamire scored 24 points, including his team's last seven, leading the Toronto Raptors to their first-ever win over the Portland Trail Blazers, 94-92.

The Raptors led by as many as 11 points with 7:57 left in the fourth quarter after a Stoudamire layup. The Trailblazers used a 13-4 run to get within a basket, 87-85, with 4:37 left. A three-pointer bomb and a pair of running jumpers by Stoudamire held off the Blazers.
"We waited too long to play the game and they came here to play," said Portland's Kenny Anderson. Isiah Rider scored 23 points to lead Portland, who had won seven of eight games.
In Dallas, Hakeem Olajuwon scored 26 points, grabbed 12 rebounds, blocked seven shots and added four assists to lead the Houston Rockets to an 88-78 win over the Dallas Mavericks.
Sam Mack added a season-high 13 points for the Rockets. Olajuwon and Mack combined to score 10 points during a 12-2 fourth-quarter run that broke the game open.
"Dream (Olajuwon) was amazing at both ends of the court," said Rockets coach Rudy Tomjanovich, whose team played without Charles Barkley, out with a sprained ankle.
Jamal Mashburn had 17 points, six rebounds, five steals and four assists for the Mavs.
In Philadelphia, Kendall Gill scored 29 points, including a dunk with 46 seconds remaining in overtime that lifted the New Jersey Nets to a 105-103 win over the Philadelphia 76ers.

Gill made a 24-footer as the Nets tied the score, 103-103, with 1:08 left in overtime. Gill then stole the ball from former Net Rex Walters at the top of the key and drove for the winning points as New Jersey ended a four-game losing streak.
In San Antonio, Sean Elliott scored 19 points and Carl Herrera added 14 as the San Antonio Spurs ended a six-game losing streak with a 96-76 rout of the Sacramento Kings.
Corliss Williamson scored 16 points for the Kings.

In Seattle, Shawn Kemp scored 22 of his 27 points in the second half as the Seattle SuperSonics remained perfect in the new year, knocking off the Cleveland Cavaliers 96-84 for their seventh straight victory.
Gary Payton added 23 points for the winners.
Chris Mills scored 21 points to pace the Cavs' attack.
At Indiana, Latrell Sprewell and Joe Smith scored 26 points apiece to lead the Golden State Warriors to a 98-91 road win over the Indiana Pacers.
Golden State hit 28-of-30 free throws, with Smith, who pulled down 11 rebounds, a perfect 10-for-10 and Sprewell going 9-for-10. Indiana was woeful from the line, hitting just 16-of-32 shots.
